habits: Build a small home lab (an old laptop or free virtual machines is enough) and write up what you try.
Do beginner capture-the-flag challenges and keep a simple public portfolio of what you learned.
Go to a local ISSA, ISACA, OWASP or BSides meeting. Most are free for students, and many jobs come from people you meet there.

roles.name: SOC Analyst
roles.tagline: The organization's lookout: you watch for signs of trouble and raise the alarm.
roles.summary: A Security Operations Center (SOC) analyst watches alerts from an organization's computers and networks, decides which ones are real problems, and passes serious ones to responders. It is the most common first job in cybersecurity.
day: Review a queue of alerts and decide which are false alarms and which need action
Look up a suspicious email, website or file to see whether it is harmful
Write short notes so the next shift knows what happened
roles.feeder: IT help desk or support roles are the usual way in, but many SOCs hire graduates directly.
steps: Learn the basics of networks and operating systems (CompTIA Network+ material is a good map).
Practice reading alerts on free blue-team labs.
Earn one starter certification, then apply to SOC, security operations and managed security provider jobs.

roles.name: Penetration Tester

roles.name: Network and Systems Security Administrator
roles.tagline: The keeper of the systems: you run networks and servers and keep them secure.
roles.summary: Network and systems administrators keep an organization's computers, servers, accounts and networks running, updated and secure. It is one of the most common doors into cybersecurity, and the skills carry into almost every other role.
day: Install security updates across hundreds of computers
Set up accounts and permissions for a new employee
Fix a network problem stopping an office from working
roles.feeder: IT support and help desk are the usual first jobs; many graduates start here directly.
steps: Learn networking basics and practice in a free network simulator.
Get comfortable with the Linux and Windows command line.
Apply to IT support, systems administrator and network technician roles.
certsLater: CompTIA Security+, then a specialist certification

roles.name: OT / ICS Security Specialist
roles.tagline: The infrastructure protector: you secure power, water and factory systems.
roles.summary: Operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) run power grids, water treatment, pipelines and factories. Specialists here protect equipment where a cyberattack can cause physical harm, so safety and reliability come first.
day: Map which plant machines are connected to which networks
Plan a security update that cannot interrupt production
Work with engineers to separate safety systems from office networks
roles.feeder: Often reached from controls engineering, field technician or IT and security roles in utilities and manufacturing.
steps: Learn how industrial systems differ from office IT.
Take CISA's free industrial control systems training.
Look at utilities, manufacturers and engineering firms, which often train new hires.

roles.name: AI Security Specialist
roles.tagline: The new frontier: you find ways AI systems can be tricked and help make them safer.
nice: No single NICE work role yet; draws on Vulnerability Analysis and Secure Software Development
roles.summary: AI security specialists test and protect AI systems such as chatbots and machine learning models: tricking them into misbehaving, stopping data leaks and defending against attacks that target the models themselves. The field is new, so few entry-level postings exist yet.
day: Try to trick a company's chatbot into revealing private data
Review how an AI feature handles untrusted input
Write guidance for teams building with AI
roles.feeder: Usually reached from AppSec, machine learning engineering, data science or SOC roles.
steps: Learn how AI language models work at a basic level.
Play free prompt-injection games and write up what worked.
Build a security foundation first; most AI security work rests on it.
roles.certsNote: No widely recognized entry certification yet; focus on projects
certsLater: CompTIA SecAI+ (launched February 2026; CompTIA recommends 3 to 4 years in IT and 2+ in security)
